tip: Write blockers as a requested action with an owner and due date.
best_tools: Notion: Maintains recurring status reports with linked tasks and owners.; ChatGPT: Condenses raw notes into clear outcome-focused updates.
prompt:
You are an operations communicator converting raw weekly notes into a report a busy stakeholder can scan in two minutes.

Project and period: [PROJECT_PERIOD]
Planned outcomes: [PLANNED]
Work completed: [COMPLETED]
Metrics or evidence: [EVIDENCE]
Work in progress: [IN_PROGRESS]
Blockers and risks: [BLOCKERS]
Decisions or help needed: [REQUESTS]
Next week's commitments: [NEXT]

Produce a one-page update beginning with a traffic-light status and a one-sentence reason. Do not choose green merely because the team was busy; compare progress with the stated plan. Organize the body into outcomes delivered, evidence, variances, blockers, decisions needed, and next commitments.

Rewrite activities as outcomes only where the notes support that interpretation. Preserve exact dates and numbers. For each blocker, name impact, owner, requested action, and decision date. For next week, limit commitments to a realistic set and use observable completion language.

Add a “changed since last report” strip and identify any item that has remained blocked for more than one period. If essential information is absent, insert [UPDATE NEEDED] instead of inventing progress. End with a three-line version suitable for a team chat and a private checklist of follow-ups for the report owner.

title: Local Shop Campaign Angle Lab
usage: Use to brainstorm practical campaign angles for a neighborhood business.
expected_output: Ten distinct campaign angles and three low-cost test plans.
tip: Test one angle with a small audience before producing a full campaign.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Generates and compares varied campaign angles from local context.; Canva: Turns selected angles into affordable social and print assets.
prompt:
Act as a practical campaign strategist for a local shop, working with real customer habits rather than big-brand clichés.

Shop type and location: [SHOP_LOCATION]
Best products or services: [OFFERINGS]
Typical customers: [CUSTOMERS]
Occasion or business goal: [GOAL]
Differentiators with proof: [PROOF]
Budget, channels, and timeframe: [CONSTRAINTS]
Languages used by customers: [LANGUAGES]

Generate ten campaign angles from distinct motivations: convenience, trust, discovery, gifting, seasonal need, community, craftsmanship, value, routine, and transformation. If one motivation does not fit, replace it with a better local insight. For every angle, provide a human truth, a one-line promise, proof required, sample headline, visual idea, suitable channel, and risk of becoming generic.

Do not assume all Pakistani customers share one culture, income, language, or religious practice. Avoid fake discounts, unsupported “best” claims, pressure tactics, and festivals not relevant to the supplied calendar. Use Urdu or regional-language phrases only when the user supplies or verifies them.

Score the angles for distinctiveness, credibility, affordability, and fit. Select three for small tests and design each test with one asset, audience, duration, response measure, and learning question. Conclude with what customer information would improve the next round.

title: Spreadsheet Cleaning Blueprint
usage: Use to plan safe cleaning before changing a messy spreadsheet.
expected_output: A staged cleaning plan with rules, checks, and rollback safeguards.
tip: Never clean the only copy; preserve a read-only raw tab with an import date.
best_tools: Excel/Sheets: Provides filters, formulas, validation, and reproducible cleaning steps.; ChatGPT: Helps diagnose column issues and draft transformation logic.
prompt:
Work as a cautious data steward planning a spreadsheet cleanup that can be audited and reversed.

File purpose: [PURPOSE]
Columns and sample rows: [SCHEMA_SAMPLE]
Known problems: [PROBLEMS]
Intended analysis: [ANALYSIS]
Tool: [EXCEL_OR_SHEETS]
Locale, date, and number conventions: [LOCALE]

Do not clean values immediately. First profile each column by expected type, missingness, uniqueness, range, pattern, and likely business rule. Build an issue register covering duplicate rows, inconsistent categories, whitespace, casing, dates, decimal separators, units, impossible values, broken formulas, and personally identifying data.

Propose a staged workflow: preserve raw import, create a working copy, standardize formats, map categories, handle missing values, resolve duplicates, validate relationships, and publish a clean table. For every transformation, state the rule, example before/after, formula or menu approach appropriate to the named tool, and rollback method. Never recommend deleting an outlier solely because it looks unusual.

Define reconciliation checks: row count, unique key count, totals before/after, unmatched mappings, formula error count, and spot-check sample. Mark decisions that require a domain owner. Finish with a data dictionary template and a cleaning log containing date, operator, rule, affected rows, and approval.

title: Chart to Decision Narrative
usage: Use to explain a chart in plain language without overstating it.
expected_output: A chart narrative with takeaway, caveats, and decision implications.
tip: Read the narrative beside the chart and verify every directional claim.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Synthesizes supplied chart details into an audience-aware narrative.; Excel/Sheets: Allows direct verification of values, labels, and chart construction.
prompt:
You are a data interpreter writing the honest story of a chart for a non-specialist decision-maker.

Chart or data: [CHART_DATA]
Metric definition: [METRIC]
Audience and decision: [AUDIENCE_DECISION]
Comparison period: [PERIOD]
Source and caveats: [SOURCE_CAVEATS]

Inspect the evidence in four passes. First describe only what is visible: level, direction, variation, and notable comparisons. Second identify the strongest decision-relevant pattern with exact values and units. Third test that pattern against base effects, seasonality, denominators, target changes, missing periods, small samples, and category redefinitions. Fourth consider at least one plausible alternative explanation.

Write three narrative layers: a 12-word chart headline, a 60-word executive explanation, and a 150-word analytical note. Each must distinguish observation from interpretation and implication. If the data does not support a firm conclusion, use appropriately cautious language rather than manufacturing certainty.

Add two annotations that should appear on the chart, one question the audience is likely to ask, and the precise additional data needed to answer it. Conclude with a decision statement formatted as “This evidence supports [ACTION] within [BOUNDARY], while we monitor [UNCERTAINTY].” Do not infer causation from timing alone.

title: Assumptions First Analysis
usage: Use before quantitative analysis to expose definitions, assumptions, and decision thresholds.
expected_output: An analysis contract with assumptions, tests, and stop conditions.
tip: Ask the decision owner to approve definitions before calculating results.
best_tools: Claude: Handles complex analytical context and tracks assumptions across a long brief.; ChatGPT: Structures decision questions, sensitivity tests, and evidence gaps.
prompt:
Act as an analytical reviewer who pauses calculation until the question and assumptions are explicit.

Decision to be made: [DECISION]
Available data: [DATA]
Proposed method: [METHOD]
Stakeholders: [STAKEHOLDERS]
Constraints: [CONSTRAINTS]
Deadline: [DEADLINE]

Produce an “analysis contract.” Define the outcome variable, unit of analysis, population, comparison, time window, success threshold, and decision rule. Then create an assumption ledger grouped into data quality, measurement, sampling, method, external conditions, and stakeholder values. For each assumption, state why it matters, current evidence, confidence, and how failure would bias the result.

Identify the five assumptions with the highest combination of uncertainty and decision impact. Design a sensitivity test or validation check for each. Draw a boundary between questions the data can answer, questions it can only indicate, and questions it cannot address.

Propose the smallest defensible analysis sequence, including baseline, segmentation, robustness checks, and uncertainty reporting. Add stop conditions for data that is too incomplete or definitions that remain unresolved. End with a pre-analysis sign-off containing choices the decision owner must confirm. Do not perform calculations or invent missing values unless explicitly asked after this framing is approved.

title: Notion Database System Designer
usage: Use to design a practical Notion database before building views and automations.
expected_output: A build-ready Notion schema with views, templates, and governance.
tip: Start with one source-of-truth database and add relations only for repeated entities.
best_tools: Notion: Supports linked databases, templates, filtered views, and team workflows.; ChatGPT: Translates workflow requirements into a clear database specification.
prompt:
Take the role of a Notion systems designer building the smallest database structure that supports the real workflow.

What is being tracked: [ITEMS]
Users and roles: [USERS]
Workflow stages: [STAGES]
Questions users need answered: [QUESTIONS]
Existing databases: [EXISTING]
Reporting or automation needs: [NEEDS]

Start by identifying the primary record and its unique naming rule. Decide whether the solution needs one database or related databases; justify every relation. Specify each property with name, type, purpose, required/optional status, allowed values, example, and owner. Avoid redundant properties that can be derived or rolled up.

Design views around user decisions: personal queue, team board, calendar, review list, and archive only where relevant. For each view, provide filter, sort, grouping, visible properties, and intended user. Create two database templates with default fields, prompts, and checklists. Add formulas only as plain-language logic unless [FORMULA_SYNTAX] is requested.

Define lifecycle rules for creation, status changes, stale records, permissions, archive, and deletion. Include one migration plan for current data and a five-record pilot test. Finish with a build order and identify nice-to-have features to postpone. Do not suggest automations that Notion cannot perform without a confirmed integration.

title: Meeting Notes to Accountable Actions
usage: Use to convert messy meeting notes into decisions, tasks, and open questions.
expected_output: A decision log, action register, and concise follow-up message.
tip: Send the action list within the same day while context is fresh.
best_tools: Notion: Stores meeting records and links actions to team workflows.; ChatGPT: Separates decisions, actions, and unresolved issues from raw notes.
prompt:
Act as a precise meeting secretary turning rough notes into accountable follow-through without filling gaps from imagination.

Meeting notes or transcript: [NOTES]
Meeting purpose: [PURPOSE]
Participant names and roles: [PARTICIPANTS]
Project context: [CONTEXT]

Separate the material into five buckets: decisions made, action items, open questions, risks or blockers, and contextual discussion. A decision must state what was agreed and, if present, why. An action must begin with a verb and include owner, deliverable, due date, dependency, and completion evidence. If any field was not explicitly agreed, write [CONFIRM] rather than assigning it.

Detect conflicting statements, tentative language, and decisions that appear to have been reopened later in the meeting. Quote a short source phrase beside ambiguous items so participants can resolve them. Exclude conversational filler and do not transform every suggestion into a task.

Produce a compact decision log followed by the action register in priority order. Add an “awaiting confirmation” section and a parking-lot list. Finish with a neutral follow-up message that summarizes the top decisions, asks owners to confirm actions, and names the next checkpoint. Preserve sensitive material only if it is necessary for execution.

title: Zapier or Make Workflow Sketch
usage: Use to map an automation before connecting live accounts or customer data.
expected_output: A workflow map with fields, branches, safeguards, and test cases.
tip: Test with fake records before granting access to production accounts.
best_tools: Zapier/Make: Connects supported apps through triggers, actions, filters, and branching.; Notion: Documents the automation specification, test cases, and ownership.
prompt:
Work as an automation architect sketching the logic before anyone connects production systems.

Desired outcome: [OUTCOME]
Triggering app and event: [TRIGGER]
Source fields: [SOURCE_FIELDS]
Destination apps and actions: [DESTINATIONS]
Conditions or approvals: [CONDITIONS]
Expected volume and urgency: [VOLUME]
Sensitive data: [SENSITIVE_DATA]

Map the workflow as numbered nodes: trigger, validation, lookup, transformation, filter, branch, action, confirmation, and logging. Use only the node types actually required. At each node, list input fields, output fields, matching key, required condition, and what happens if data is blank, duplicated, malformed, delayed, or rejected.

Compare a Zapier-style linear design with a Make-style scenario when branching or iteration is involved, but do not claim a connector or feature exists unless the user confirms it. Identify human approval points for payments, public messages, record deletion, or consequential decisions.

Add safeguards for least-privilege access, test data, idempotency, duplicate prevention, rate limits, retry behavior, error notification, audit log, and manual recovery. Provide five test cases including happy path, duplicate, missing field, app outage, and unauthorized value. Finish with implementation order, owner, monitoring cadence, and a rollback switch. Never place passwords or API keys in the specification.

title: KPI Definition Card Maker
usage: Use to define KPIs consistently before building a dashboard.
expected_output: Standard KPI cards and a metric governance checklist.
tip: Calculate one example by hand with the metric owner before publishing.
best_tools: Excel/Sheets: Documents metric formulas and validates sample calculations transparently.; Notion: Maintains a shared KPI dictionary with owners and revision history.
prompt:
You are a measurement lead defining KPIs so two analysts calculate the same answer from the same data.

Business objective: [OBJECTIVE]
Proposed KPI names: [KPIS]
Available systems: [SYSTEMS]
Reporting audience: [AUDIENCE]
Review frequency: [FREQUENCY]
Known disputes: [DISPUTES]

For each KPI, create a definition card containing: decision it informs, plain-language meaning, exact formula, numerator, denominator, unit, inclusion rules, exclusion rules, time window, segment dimensions, source system, refresh timing, data owner, business owner, target source, and known limitations. Clarify whether the metric is leading, lagging, diagnostic, or guardrail.

Include a worked example using clearly labelled sample numbers, then test edge cases such as zero denominator, late-arriving records, cancellations, duplicates, and timezone boundaries. If a term like “active,” “customer,” or “completed” appears, demand an operational definition.

Compare any KPIs that may conflict or encourage harmful gaming. Recommend one balancing metric where needed. Finish with a compact KPI dictionary, a change-control rule for revised definitions, and five dashboard footnotes users may need. Do not choose targets without evidence or present an attractive number as useful if it does not inform action.

title: Unbiased Survey Designer
usage: Use to design a short survey that measures one clear research objective.
expected_output: A field-ready survey instrument with rationale and pilot checks.
tip: Pilot with five people and ask what they thought each question meant.
best_tools: Google Forms: Builds accessible surveys with common question types and branching.; Microsoft Forms: Supports straightforward organizational survey collection and export.
prompt:
Act as a survey methodologist designing the shortest instrument that can answer [RESEARCH_OBJECTIVE].

Target population: [POPULATION]
Sampling and distribution plan: [SAMPLING]
Decisions based on results: [DECISIONS]
Required topics: [TOPICS]
Languages and accessibility needs: [LANGUAGES_ACCESS]
Maximum completion time: [TIME]
Sensitive questions: [SENSITIVE]

Begin with a construct map: what must be measured, what is merely interesting, and what should be excluded. Then draft the survey in respondent order: brief consent and purpose, screening if necessary, easy behavioral questions, core measures, optional open text, demographics only when analytically justified, and close.

Use one idea per question. Avoid leading, loaded, double-barrelled, absolute, and hypothetical wording. For every closed question, provide balanced response options, an appropriate recall period, and “not applicable/prefer not to answer” where needed. Do not use agreement scales when a direct frequency or quality measure is clearer.

Annotate each question privately with purpose, variable type, and planned analysis. Add branch logic and randomization only when justified. Estimate completion time, then design a five-person cognitive pilot with probes for comprehension and response fit. End with privacy, translation/back-translation, mobile display, missing-data, and reporting checks. Do not promise anonymity if collection settings cannot guarantee it.

title: Spreadsheet Error Check Formulas
usage: Use to design formula-based checks that flag likely spreadsheet errors.
expected_output: A formula check library with test cases and review guidance.
tip: Keep every flag column visible during testing and investigate false positives.
best_tools: Excel/Sheets: Supports transparent formulas, validation rules, and conditional formatting.; ChatGPT: Drafts formula patterns from a supplied schema and business rules.
prompt:
Work as a spreadsheet quality reviewer proposing checks that flag anomalies without silently changing data.

Tool and version: [EXCEL_OR_SHEETS]
Column letters/names: [SCHEMA]
Sample rows: [SAMPLES]
Business rules: [RULES]
Known errors: [KNOWN_ERRORS]
Locale separators: [LOCALE]

Design a set of helper-column checks for required blanks, duplicate keys, invalid categories, text where numbers are expected, impossible date order, out-of-range values, inconsistent units, cross-column mismatch, formula errors, and broken totals. Include only checks relevant to the supplied schema.

For each check, give a plain-language rule, formula using the exact supplied columns, expected TRUE/FALSE or message output, one passing example, one failing example, and what a reviewer should do. Prefer readable formulas and explain compatibility differences between Excel and Google Sheets. Where a formula depends on modern functions, offer a simpler fallback.

Add a summary section that counts each error type and highlights rows through conditional formatting without hiding source values. Distinguish hard errors from warnings. Recommend testing formulas on a copy, locking reference ranges where needed, and manually verifying a sample. If schema details are missing, provide formula pseudocode with [COLUMN] placeholders instead of guessing.

title: Personal Knowledge Base Architecture
usage: Use to create a simple knowledge system you can maintain each week.
expected_output: A maintainable knowledge-base structure with templates and routines.
tip: Design around how you will retrieve notes, then limit capture fields.
best_tools: Notion: Combines notes, linked databases, templates, and searchable project context.; Obsidian: Supports local markdown notes and lightweight linking between ideas.
prompt:
Act as a personal knowledge systems coach designing for retrieval, reflection, and action—not endless note collecting.

Main uses: [USES]
Current tools and notes: [CURRENT_SYSTEM]
Types of information captured: [INFORMATION]
Weekly maintenance time: [TIME]
Privacy or offline needs: [PRIVACY]
Preferred tool: [NOTION_OR_OBSIDIAN]

Define four flows: capture, clarify, connect, and retrieve. Propose the smallest folder or database architecture that supports those flows. Separate time-bound projects, ongoing responsibilities, reference material, and original insights without forcing every note into many categories.

Create templates for quick capture, source note, concept note, meeting/lecture note, and weekly review. Each template should have only fields that improve future search or use. Provide a naming convention, tag policy with a maximum number of tag families, linking rule, and source-citation habit. Explain how the design differs in Notion and Obsidian where relevant.

Map a 15-minute weekly review: process inbox, link useful notes, surface open questions, archive stale material, and choose one idea to apply. Include a migration plan that starts with active material rather than importing everything. Finish with three retrieval tests the system must pass after two weeks and warning signs that the structure has become too complex.

title: Word Rewrite With Guardrails
usage: Rewrite a Word document while preserving meaning, facts, and the writer's natural voice.
expected_output: A polished rewrite plus a concise change log for human review.
tip: Save the original as a separate version before accepting broad changes.
best_tools: Microsoft Copilot: Works directly with selected text and surrounding Word document context.
prompt:
Role: You are my careful in-document editor; your goal is to improve this Word draft without changing its facts or personality.

Work only from [SELECTED_TEXT] and, where relevant, [DOCUMENT_CONTEXT]. The intended reader is [AUDIENCE], the purpose is [PURPOSE], and the desired tone is [TONE]. Keep names, dates, figures, commitments, citations, and technical terms exactly as supplied unless you flag a likely error instead of silently correcting it.

Rewrite in two passes. First, remove repetition, vague phrasing, and unnecessarily long sentences. Second, check flow between paragraphs and strengthen headings or transitions where needed. Preserve deliberate cultural references and Pakistani English usage unless [LANGUAGE_PREFERENCE] says otherwise.

Return:
- the revised text, ready to paste;
- five or fewer notable edits with short reasons;
- a “Check manually” list for claims, quotations, or ambiguous wording.

Do not invent evidence or make the prose sound generically corporate. If an instruction conflicts with the original meaning, retain the meaning and note the conflict.

title: Excel Analysis Question Designer
usage: Ask Copilot in Excel for a focused, auditable analysis of a selected table.
expected_output: An analysis plan, formulas or pivots, findings, and validation checks.
tip: Convert the range to a named table and define each column before asking.
best_tools: Microsoft Copilot: Can analyze structured workbook tables and suggest formulas or summaries in context.

title: Gmail Context-Aware Draft
usage: Draft a clear Gmail reply grounded in the thread and the sender's actual request.
expected_output: A concise email draft with subject, action, and verification flags.
tip: Recheck recipients, attachments, dates, and promises before pressing Send.
best_tools: Gemini in Gmail: Uses the open email thread as context for drafting and summarising.

title: Grammarly Plus Human Tone Review
usage: Run a Grammarly tone pass, then complete a disciplined human editorial check.
expected_output: A revised passage and a checked editorial decision log.
tip: Reject any suggestion that changes responsibility, certainty, or the author's intended voice.
best_tools: Grammarly: Highlights grammar, clarity, and tone signals directly in the writing surface.

title: Browser Sidebar Research Capture Card
usage: Capture a web source into reusable evidence notes without confusing claims with conclusions.
expected_output: A source card with claims, quotes, limitations, and follow-up questions.
tip: Open the original source and verify quotations instead of trusting the sidebar summary.
best_tools: Browser AI sidebar: Can summarise the open page while keeping its URL and visible context nearby.

title: GitHub Copilot Function Scaffold
usage: Generate a function stub with explicit contracts, edge cases, and test placeholders.
expected_output: A typed function skeleton, documentation, validation, and test cases.
tip: Keep the TODOs until each assumption has a matching test or documented decision.
best_tools: GitHub Copilot: Uses nearby code, types, and conventions to propose an in-editor scaffold.

title: Cursor Multi-File Refactor Brief
usage: Ask Cursor to refactor several files while preserving public behavior and limiting scope.
expected_output: A scoped refactor, affected-file summary, and test evidence.
tip: Name the permitted files and verification command before authorising edits.
best_tools: Cursor: Can inspect related files and apply coordinated edits across a codebase.

title: Notion Meeting Notes Curator
usage: Convert rough Notion meeting notes into decisions, actions, questions, and a concise record.
expected_output: A structured meeting record with traceable actions and unresolved items.
tip: Ask participants to confirm owners and deadlines after the cleanup.
best_tools: Notion AI: Can restructure notes directly within a shared Notion workspace page.
prompt:
Goal: Curate [RAW_MEETING_NOTES] into a reliable Notion meeting record that distinguishes what happened from what remains uncertain.

Use the meeting name [MEETING_NAME], date [DATE], and participant list [PARTICIPANTS]. Begin with a three-line overview covering purpose, main outcome, and current status. Then sort the notes into: decisions confirmed, action items, open questions, discussion highlights, and parking-lot topics.

Format each action as a Notion-friendly checklist containing one deliverable, one owner, and one deadline. If any element is missing, use “unassigned” or “date not agreed”; never infer responsibility from who spoke. Mark contradictory notes with a ⚠ review label and quote both versions briefly.

Create a compact decision log with the decision, rationale stated in the notes, decision-maker if known, and reconsideration trigger. Remove filler and duplicate fragments, but retain dissent, risks, and important context.

Conclude with a follow-up message that can be pasted to participants, asking them to confirm corrections by [CONFIRMATION_DATE]. Do not add absent commitments or portray proposals as approvals.

title: Study Pack Production Pipeline
usage: Design a multi-tool pipeline that turns learning material into an ethical study pack.
expected_output: A sequenced workflow with tools, handoffs, quality gates, and file names.
tip: Keep source citations attached to notes throughout every transformation.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Coordinates staged transformations and produces clear reusable instructions.
prompt:
Role: You are a learning-workflow designer; map a responsible study-pack pipeline for [SUBJECT] and [LEARNER_LEVEL].

The available inputs are [SOURCE_MATERIALS], the deadline is [DEADLINE], and permitted tools are [AVAILABLE_TOOLS]. Design a sequence that may use document extraction, an AI assistant, flashcard software, and a word processor, but assign each tool only work it performs well. Describe what moves between tools and in which format.

Include stages for source inventory, concept mapping, plain-language notes, worked examples, retrieval questions, flashcards, a timed revision plan, and final fact-checking against original material. Insert a human approval gate before generated content becomes a study aid. Do not create answer keys for live tests or suggest bypassing academic rules.

For every stage specify: input, action, tool choice, output filename, and quality check. Show how to preserve page numbers or links so claims remain traceable. Offer a low-tech alternative where a proposed integration is unavailable.

Finish with a folder structure and a 30-minute maintenance routine. Optimise for understanding and recall, not volume of generated notes.

title: Monthly Content Calendar Pipeline
usage: Build a repeatable workflow from audience insight to approved, scheduled content.
expected_output: A month-long content workflow with handoffs, controls, and metrics.
tip: Separate factual review from style approval so neither becomes a quick checkbox.
best_tools: Claude: Handles long brand context and can organise a detailed editorial workflow.
prompt:
Goal: Engineer a content-calendar pipeline for [BRAND] that produces [CHANNELS] content for [AUDIENCE] during [MONTH].

Start with an insight intake from [CUSTOMER_QUESTIONS], performance data, seasonal moments, and business priorities. Explain how a spreadsheet or database stores ideas, an AI assistant clusters themes, a writing tool develops drafts, a design tool creates assets, and a scheduler publishes approved items. Avoid assuming direct integrations; describe manual handoffs where necessary.

Create a weekly cadence from research through retrospective. Define status labels, naming rules, owners, and minimum information required before an idea advances. Add approval gates for claims, brand voice, accessibility, image rights, and sensitive topics. AI may suggest language, but [APPROVER] owns final publication.

Recommend a balanced content mix rather than repeating one format. For each stage, state the artifact produced, the receiving tool, and a failure check—for example, unsupported statistics or cropped captions.

End with five useful performance signals and a monthly learning loop showing how results influence the next calendar without chasing vanity metrics.

title: AI-Assisted Client Delivery Checklist
usage: Create a controlled client-delivery process with transparent and reviewable AI assistance.
expected_output: A stage-gated checklist from intake through handover and retention.
tip: Remove confidential identifiers before any tool not approved by the client.
best_tools: Microsoft Copilot: Supports documents, spreadsheets, email, and presentations in a connected work environment.
prompt:
Role: Operate as a client-delivery quality manager; build a checklist for [SERVICE] from signed brief to final handover.

Account for [CLIENT_REQUIREMENTS], [DELIVERABLES], [DEADLINE], and [APPROVED_AI_TOOLS]. Divide the workflow into intake, scope confirmation, source collection, production, internal review, client review, revision control, delivery, and closeout. At each stage, identify where AI can assist and where a named human must decide.

Provide checklist items for consent, data classification, redaction, prompt logging if required, factual verification, accessibility, brand compliance, and version naming. Include a stop condition when confidential data, unclear ownership, or out-of-scope requests appear. Generated work must never be described as independently verified.

Define the handoff artifact between tools—such as a sanitised brief, draft document, issue log, or approved PDF—and who accepts it. Add a change-request route that records impact on timeline and scope.

Finish with a delivery manifest listing files, versions, approvals, unresolved limitations, and retention or deletion actions. Make the checklist usable in [PROJECT_PLATFORM].

title: Source-to-Decision Brief Workflow
usage: Plan a traceable path from research question to concise decision brief.
expected_output: A research workflow with an evidence ledger and decision-ready brief.
tip: Treat search summaries as leads and verify important claims in original sources.
best_tools: Perplexity: Helps discover web sources and provides links that can be independently checked.
prompt:
Goal: Design a research-to-brief workflow that answers [DECISION_QUESTION] for [DECISION_MAKER] by [DEADLINE].

Begin by converting the question into scope boundaries, decision criteria, search concepts, and exclusion rules. Assign discovery to [SEARCH_TOOL], source capture to [NOTES_TOOL], comparison to [ANALYSIS_TOOL], and drafting to [WRITING_TOOL]. Explain each handoff in terms of data fields, not vague “integration.”

Require an evidence ledger containing URL or document ID, publisher, date, claim, quotation or location, geography, method, limitations, and verification status. Include a deliberate search for disagreement and missing perspectives. High-impact claims need either a primary source or two independent credible sources.

Describe how to move from evidence clusters to findings, then from findings to options with trade-offs. Add checkpoints for stale information, duplicated reporting, unsupported causality, and confidence calibration.

Specify the final brief sections and a one-page limit for its executive layer. Close with an audit step where another person can trace every material sentence back to the ledger and mark unresolved uncertainty.

title: Focused Job-Hunt Daily System
usage: Organise a daily job search across discovery, tailoring, outreach, tracking, and follow-up.
expected_output: A time-boxed daily workflow and an application tracking system.
tip: Never let AI add experience, credentials, or results that you cannot evidence.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can coordinate tailoring, rehearsal, planning, and reflection from supplied information.
prompt:
Role: Be my job-search operations coach; create a daily workflow for [TARGET_ROLES] in [LOCATION_OR_REMOTE_PREFERENCE].

I have [DAILY_TIME] available and use [JOB_BOARDS], [DOCUMENT_TOOL], [AI_ASSISTANT], and [TRACKER]. Divide the session into opportunity discovery, fit screening, CV tailoring, cover note preparation, networking, application submission, and follow-up. Give each block a realistic time limit and a definition of done.

Build a fit score using essential skills, evidence from my background [CANDIDATE_PROFILE], location, work arrangement, and genuine interest. Reject roles with material mismatches instead of forcing keywords. Describe how AI may compare documents or rehearse messages but must not invent qualifications, referrals, salary history, or employer research.

Define tracker columns for source, deadline, tailored files, contact, status, next action, and outcome. Include file naming and a pre-submit check for dates, company name, links, claims, and attachments.

End with a 10-minute review that captures one lesson, schedules follow-ups, and adjusts tomorrow's search terms without measuring success only by application count.

title: Small Business Weekly AI Rhythm
usage: Plan a practical weekly AI routine for a small business with clear human controls.
expected_output: A weekday routine with inputs, owners, outputs, and safety checks.
tip: Start with one repeated bottleneck and measure saved rework, not generated volume.
best_tools: Gemini: Can support planning and drafting across common Google Workspace workflows.
prompt:
Goal: Build a weekly AI operating rhythm for [BUSINESS_TYPE] serving [CUSTOMERS] with a team of [TEAM_SIZE].

Use our recurring responsibilities [WEEKLY_TASKS], approved tools [TOOLS], and constraints [CONSTRAINTS]. Assign one theme to each working day: planning and demand review, customer communication, marketing production, operations improvement, and finance or performance reflection. Adapt the pattern if [WORKING_DAYS] differs.

For each activity, show the source information, AI-assisted action, human owner, output, and approval rule. Include low-risk uses such as summarising non-sensitive feedback and drafting alternatives, while blocking entry of CNICs, payment details, passwords, private employee records, or confidential client material into unapproved systems.

Add a reusable prompt log and a simple “keep, change, stop” review. Flag tasks requiring professional judgement or current official information. Prevent automation from sending customer messages or changing records without confirmation.

Conclude with three measures: turnaround time, error or rework rate, and customer outcome. Recommend only [MAX_EXPERIMENTS] experiments for the first month so the routine remains manageable.

title: Data-to-Decision Operating Workflow
usage: Turn operational data into a documented recommendation with validation and accountability.
expected_output: A controlled analytical workflow ending in a decision record.
tip: Reconcile totals to the source system before discussing trends.
best_tools: Microsoft Copilot: Works across spreadsheet analysis, written summaries, and presentation preparation.
prompt:
Role: Act as an analytics process designer; map how [DATASET] should inform [DECISION] without overstating certainty.

Identify the source system, data owner, refresh date, unit of analysis, and decision deadline. Lay out a sequence using [DATA_TOOL] for cleaning, [ANALYSIS_TOOL] for calculation, [WRITING_TOOL] for the decision memo, and [PRESENTATION_TOOL] only if stakeholders need it. Every handoff must retain dataset version and filter definitions.

Insert controls for duplicates, missing values, outliers, unit mismatches, denominator changes, and reconciliation to known totals. Distinguish descriptive findings, forecasts, and causal claims. Require sensitivity checks for [KEY_ASSUMPTIONS] and segment results where averages could hide material differences.

The workflow should produce an analysis notebook or formula record, a chart pack, a finding log, and a recommendation with options. Assign a challenger to test alternative explanations before approval.

Finish with a decision register capturing owner, date, evidence used, assumptions, chosen option, rejected alternatives, review trigger, and later outcome. Include a route to say “insufficient evidence” rather than manufacturing confidence.

title: Teacher Preparation Workflow
usage: Prepare an inclusive lesson through curriculum alignment, resource creation, review, and reflection.
expected_output: A tool-by-tool lesson preparation process with teacher review gates.
tip: Test every generated example for age, culture, language, and curriculum fit.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Supports lesson ideation, differentiation, question design, and structured reflection.
prompt:
Goal: Design a teaching-preparation workflow for [TOPIC], [GRADE_OR_LEVEL], and a [LESSON_DURATION] session.

Begin from [CURRICULUM_OUTCOME] and available resources [MATERIALS], not from an AI-generated activity. Show how the teacher defines evidence of learning, uses an assistant to brainstorm misconceptions and examples, develops slides or handouts, creates formative questions, checks accessibility, and stores approved resources in [PLATFORM].

At each stage name the input, tool, output, and teacher decision. Include differentiation for [LEARNER_NEEDS], language support, a no-device alternative, and a plan for students who finish early. Questions should assess understanding rather than reward guessing; do not generate answers for active graded assessments.

Add checks for factual accuracy, local cultural relevance, reading level, copyright, safeguarding, and accidental disclosure of student information. Any student data must be removed or anonymised before external tools are used.

End with a pre-class readiness list, a minute-by-minute lesson spine, and a post-class reflection loop that compares intended evidence with what learners actually demonstrated.

title: CSS and PMS Study Plan Builder
usage: Build a realistic CSS or PMS preparation schedule centred on concepts and ethical practice.
expected_output: A phased weekly plan with milestones, revision cycles, and progress checks.
tip: Verify the current syllabus and dates on the relevant official commission website.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can structure long-term schedules around supplied subjects, constraints, and progress.
prompt:
Role: You are an ethical CSS/PMS preparation planner; build a concept-first schedule for [EXAM], [ATTEMPT_YEAR], and [PROVINCE_IF_PMS].

Use only the officially published syllabus supplied in [SYLLABUS], my compulsory and optional subjects [SUBJECTS], current baseline [BASELINE], weekly availability [HOURS], and exam timeline [DATES]. If official dates or rules are not provided, tell me to verify them rather than guessing.

Divide preparation into foundation, coverage, consolidation, timed practice, and final revision. Allocate time by syllabus weight, difficulty, and diagnostic weakness. Include newspaper or current-affairs note-making, essay planning, précis or language practice where applicable, past-paper topic mapping, spaced recall, and weekly rest.

Provide a twelve-week view or [PLAN_LENGTH], then detail the first seven days. Set measurable milestones based on concepts mastered and practice reviewed, not hours alone. Include a recovery rule for missed sessions and a fortnightly rebalance.

Do not provide leaked material, impersonation, live-exam answers, or methods to evade rules. Past papers may be used only for legitimate practice and pattern analysis.

title: CSS and PMS Concept Self-Tutor
usage: Learn a CSS or PMS concept through explanation, examples, recall, and self-testing.
expected_output: A layered explanation followed by questions, feedback criteria, and revision cues.
tip: Answer the self-test before revealing feedback or model explanations.
best_tools: Claude: Can explain nuanced concepts and generate structured self-tests from supplied sources.
prompt:
Goal: Teach me [CONCEPT] from the [CSS_OR_PMS_SUBJECT] syllabus until I can explain and apply it independently.

Start by asking for my current understanding in two or three sentences. Then give a layered explanation: a plain-language definition, the key mechanism or argument, its Pakistan relevance where genuinely applicable, one concrete example, and one common misconception. Base the lesson on [SOURCES_OR_NOTES]; label anything that requires current verification.

Use a teach-back pause before testing me. Create six self-test items in mixed forms: recall, distinction, application, evidence evaluation, counterargument, and a short outline. Do not answer them immediately. Wait for [MY_ANSWERS], then assess each against explicit criteria, identify the misconception behind any error, and offer a targeted retry question.

Finish with a compact revision card containing five key terms, three relationships, and two credible source types to consult. This is study support only: do not answer an active examination, reproduce restricted material, or imply guaranteed marks.

title: HEC University Assignment Structure Coach
usage: Plan an original university assignment structure while preserving the student's authorship and citations.
expected_output: An assignment map with argument roles, evidence needs, and writing checkpoints.
tip: Check your own university's policy because HEC affiliation does not create one universal AI rule.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Helps interpret assignment requirements and organise arguments into a coherent plan.
prompt:
Role: Act as my academic structure coach, not my ghostwriter; help me plan [ASSIGNMENT_TOPIC] for [COURSE].

Read the exact brief [ASSIGNMENT_BRIEF], rubric [RUBRIC], required length [WORD_COUNT], citation style [STYLE], and my preliminary ideas [MY_IDEAS]. Separate explicit requirements from assumptions. If the institution's AI policy [POLICY] is unclear, advise me to ask the instructor before generating submission-ready prose.

Propose a central question and two or three possible thesis directions, showing what evidence each would require. Build a section outline with approximate word allocations, purpose of each section, claim to develop, counterpoint to consider, and placeholder citations such as [SOURCE NEEDED]. Do not invent references, quotations, data, or fieldwork.

Add a writing sequence that begins with my notes, includes source verification and paraphrase checking, and ends with a rubric-based self-review. Ask five coaching questions that force me to supply the analysis.

Keep the final output at planning level. Flag any request that would replace my own assessed learning or breach university rules.

title: Thesis Chapter Architecture Planner
usage: Design a thesis chapter map aligned with the research question, method, and evidence.
expected_output: A chapter blueprint with purposes, evidence, dependencies, and review questions.
tip: Treat supervisor guidance and departmental format as authoritative over generic conventions.
best_tools: Claude: Handles long research context and can compare argument structure across chapters.
prompt:
Goal: Serve as a thesis architecture adviser and map chapters for [DEGREE_PROGRAMME] research on [TOPIC].

Work from my research question [QUESTION], objectives [OBJECTIVES], methodology [METHOD], available evidence [EVIDENCE], theoretical frame [FRAMEWORK], and departmental requirements [GUIDELINES]. Do not assume every thesis needs the same chapter pattern.

Offer up to two viable architectures and explain when each works. For the chosen structure, define each chapter's job, central claim or contribution, inputs, planned sections, connection to the previous chapter, and evidence still needed. Show where literature is reviewed, method is justified, findings are presented, and interpretation occurs without duplicating material.

Create an argument thread that can be followed from problem to contribution. Identify dependencies—for example, analysis that cannot begin before coding—and likely scope creep. Add chapter-specific questions for a supervisor meeting and completion criteria that are stronger than word count.

Do not fabricate citations, results, participants, approvals, or quotations. Mark ethical and institutional decisions for confirmation with the supervisor or relevant review body.

title: Scholarship SOP Argument Architect
usage: Build an authentic scholarship statement structure from the applicant's verified experiences and goals.
expected_output: A tailored SOP blueprint, evidence map, and authenticity review.
tip: Replace broad claims about impact with one verifiable action, result, and lesson.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can organise personal evidence into a coherent narrative and question weak claims.
prompt:
Role: You are my scholarship SOP architect; help me design the argument while keeping every sentence truthful and recognisably mine.

Analyse [SCHOLARSHIP_PROMPT], selection criteria [CRITERIA], programme [PROGRAMME], word limit [LIMIT], and my verified experience bank [EXPERIENCES]. Identify what the reviewers actually need to learn and which of my examples can demonstrate it. Never create leadership roles, hardship, grades, awards, impact figures, or future partnerships.

Develop a narrative spine linking formative context, relevant action, learning, programme fit, and a plausible contribution after study. For each paragraph, state its purpose, best evidence, reflection angle, and transition. Include alternatives when an example is weak or overused.

Ask me focused questions where specificity is missing. Then provide an opening strategy and closing strategy as outlines, not polished autobiographical prose. Add a “proof and permission” check for facts involving other people.

Finish with a reviewer test covering fit, evidence, humility, clarity, and whether the goals make sense in Pakistan and beyond. Keep the applicant—not the AI—as the author.

title: International CV Evidence Tailor
usage: Tailor a Pakistani candidate's CV to an international vacancy without fabricating credentials.
expected_output: A tailored CV draft, evidence gaps, and a final accuracy checklist.
tip: Research destination-country conventions before including a photo, CNIC, age, or marital status.
best_tools: Microsoft Copilot: Can compare a job description with a CV and revise the document in place.
prompt:
Goal: Tailor my CV for [ROLE] in [COUNTRY_OR_MARKET] using only evidence contained in [MASTER_CV] and [ACHIEVEMENT_NOTES].

Parse [JOB_DESCRIPTION] into essential outcomes, skills, tools, seniority signals, and optional criteria. Create a match map showing strong evidence, partial evidence, and genuine gaps. Do not hide gaps with inflated synonyms or add qualifications, visa status, language fluency, team size, budgets, or metrics not supplied.

Recommend the appropriate CV order and length for the target market, noting any convention that I should independently verify. Rewrite the profile and experience bullets using action, context, and evidenced result. Preserve exact employers, titles, dates, and credentials. Use keywords naturally; do not keyword-stuff or attempt to game screening systems.

Flag Pakistani terms that international readers may not understand and suggest accurate explanations. Identify personal details that may be unnecessary or risky in the destination market.

Return the revised sections, a list of omitted low-relevance material, five interview proof points, and an accuracy checklist requiring my confirmation before submission.

title: Rozee.pk and LinkedIn Application Kit
usage: Prepare a consistent application kit for a genuine vacancy found on Rozee.pk or LinkedIn.
expected_output: A fit note, tailored profile, cover message, tracker entry, and safety flags.
tip: Verify the employer domain and never pay or share sensitive documents merely to apply.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can compare vacancy details with candidate evidence and draft coordinated materials.
prompt:
Role: Act as my Pakistan job-application desk; assemble an honest kit for [VACANCY_TEXT] found on [ROZEE_OR_LINKEDIN].

Compare the vacancy with [MY_CV] and [CAREER_GOALS]. First produce a fit verdict—apply, clarify, or skip—with evidence. Note missing salary, location, schedule, contract type, and application deadline. Flag scam indicators such as payment requests, personal email domains, pressure to share banking details, or unverifiable company identity, while acknowledging that a flag is not proof.

For a suitable role, prepare: a targeted three-line profile, six prioritised CV bullet selections or rewrites, a brief platform application message, and a respectful networking note to [CONTACT_TYPE]. Keep every claim supported by my materials and avoid generic enthusiasm.

Add a tracker row with job title, company, source URL, date found, deadline, documents used, status, and follow-up date. Include five questions to investigate before interview.

Do not submit anything, contact anyone, or disclose CNIC, bank details, passwords, or references without my explicit decision.

title: Upwork and Fiverr Proposal Proof Writer
usage: Draft a concise freelance proposal grounded in the client's brief and the seller's real proof.
expected_output: A tailored proposal, milestones, clarifying questions, and risk flags.
tip: Mention only samples you can actually share and outcomes you can substantiate.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can connect project requirements to supplied work samples and formulate clarifying questions.
prompt:
Goal: Write an evidence-based proposal for [PLATFORM] opportunity [CLIENT_BRIEF] using my actual profile [FREELANCER_PROFILE].

Diagnose the client's likely outcome, deliverables, constraints, and unanswered questions. Identify up to three genuine proof points from [WORK_SAMPLES] that are relevant; if none fit, say so rather than inventing a portfolio item. Open with a specific observation about the work, not a generic greeting or claim to be “the best.”

Draft a proposal of [LENGTH] that explains my approach, a sensible first milestone, communication rhythm, and what I need from the client. Where scope is uncertain, give conditional options instead of a fixed promise. Include three concise questions that expose important assumptions.

Add a private review section checking feasibility, timeline, ownership of source files, confidentiality, platform communication rules, and suspicious requests. Do not suggest off-platform evasion, copied samples, false testimonials, unpaid speculative work beyond a reasonable boundary, or guarantees outside my control.

End with two alternative closing lines: one direct and one warm. Preserve my natural voice [VOICE_SAMPLE].

title: Pakistan City Market Campaign Planner
usage: Plan a locally grounded campaign for a specific Pakistani city using testable assumptions.
expected_output: A city-specific campaign plan with experiments, safeguards, and measurement.
tip: Validate neighbourhood, language, and channel assumptions with real customers before launch.
best_tools: Gemini: Supports research-led planning and multilingual content ideation from supplied local context.
prompt:
Role: You are a local-market campaign strategist; plan a launch for [OFFER] in [PAKISTAN_CITY] without relying on clichés.

Use the evidence supplied in [CUSTOMER_INSIGHTS], [COMPETITOR_NOTES], [SEASON], [CHANNEL_ACCESS], and [CONSTRAINTS]. Separate known facts from hypotheses about language, neighbourhoods, purchasing power, mobility, digital behaviour, and trust. If current local data is unavailable, design a validation step rather than inventing statistics.

Define one primary audience by need and context, not broad demographics alone. Create a positioning statement, message hierarchy, channel mix, four-week activity sequence, and two language variants appropriate to [LANGUAGE_PREFERENCE]. Consider local holidays, prayer times, weather, delivery realities, and cultural sensitivities only where relevant and verified.

Propose three small experiments with hypothesis, audience, creative, success measure, and stop rule. Include community or offline options alongside digital channels. Avoid discriminatory targeting, political manipulation, spam, and unsupported health or income claims.

Finish with an approval checklist and a measurement dashboard covering qualified enquiries, conversion, repeat interest, complaints, and learning—not reach alone.

title: Urdu, English, and Roman Urdu Adapter
usage: Adapt one message across Urdu, English, and Roman Urdu while preserving intent and register.
expected_output: Three aligned language versions plus notes on ambiguity and terminology.
tip: Have a fluent human review public-facing Urdu and names written in Urdu script.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can compare multilingual phrasing and explain register choices in context.
prompt:
Goal: Adapt [SOURCE_MESSAGE] into natural Pakistani English, Urdu script, and Roman Urdu for [AUDIENCE] and [CHANNEL].

Preserve the message's intent, factual content, call to action, names, dates, amounts, and level of formality. Before translating, identify ambiguous phrases and ask for clarification if they could materially change meaning. Use [REGION_OR_REGISTER] preferences where supplied; otherwise choose widely understandable wording and label the choice.

Present the three versions in parallel sections. Do not transliterate the English mechanically: adapt idioms, greetings, honorifics, sentence length, and punctuation so each version sounds native to its medium. Keep protected terms [TERMS_TO_KEEP] unchanged and provide a short glossary for specialised vocabulary.

After the variants, explain up to five adaptation decisions, including any phrase with no exact equivalent. Flag words that may sound too formal, too casual, gendered, or region-specific. Offer one shorter option for SMS or WhatsApp if [CHARACTER_LIMIT] applies.

Do not translate legal, medical, or safety-critical wording with false confidence; mark it for qualified bilingual review.

title: WhatsApp Business Message Suite
usage: Create permission-aware WhatsApp Business messages for common customer moments.
expected_output: A labelled pack of concise templates with placeholders and escalation rules.
tip: Use approved customer lists and respect opt-outs immediately.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can draft multiple short message types from one brand and service context.
prompt:
Role: Act as a WhatsApp Business conversation designer; build a message pack for [BUSINESS] serving [CUSTOMER_TYPE].

Use the brand voice [VOICE], operating hours [HOURS], languages [LANGUAGES], and confirmed policies [POLICIES]. Draft distinct templates for first enquiry, information request, order confirmation, payment-pending reminder, delay update, appointment reminder, complaint acknowledgement, resolution follow-up, and opt-out confirmation.

Keep each message short enough for chat and give it one clear action. Use visible placeholders such as [CUSTOMER_NAME], [ORDER_ID], [DATE], and [SUPPORT_CONTACT]; never insert imagined policy details. For sensitive cases, state when a human should take over. Do not request passwords, PINs, full card details, or unnecessary CNIC images.

Provide English and [SECOND_LANGUAGE] versions where requested, adapting rather than literally translating. Mark promotional templates separately from service messages and include consent and frequency notes. Avoid pressure tactics, repeated unsolicited follow-ups, and fake scarcity.

Finish with a mini style guide covering greetings, emoji restraint, response timing, escalation, and how staff should record customer consent or opt-out.

title: FBR Tax Awareness Explainer
usage: Explain a Pakistan tax topic in plain language with official-source checks and boundaries.
expected_output: An informational overview, verification checklist, and questions for a professional.
tip: Confirm tax year, taxpayer type, and the current FBR notification before relying on any threshold.
best_tools: Perplexity: Can locate current official pages for verification while showing source links.
prompt:
Goal: Explain [PAKISTAN_TAX_TOPIC] for general awareness in plain language, using the context [TAXPAYER_SCENARIO].

Start with this exact boundary in substance: “This is general information, not tax, legal, or financial advice. Rules, rates, forms, and deadlines can change; verify current requirements with FBR and a qualified Pakistan tax professional.”

Identify the relevant tax year [TAX_YEAR], taxpayer type, and jurisdictional assumptions. Explain key terms, why the topic matters, the usual process at a high level, records commonly needed, and questions a person should clarify. Where figures, deadlines, forms, or portal steps are mentioned, cite or request a current official FBR source [OFFICIAL_SOURCES] and clearly date the information.

Separate confirmed official information from examples and general interpretation. Do not calculate a final liability, recommend concealment, invent exemptions, or present a fictional filing as compliant. Flag cases involving notices, penalties, audits, foreign income, residency, withholding disputes, or complex business structures for professional help.

End with an official-source verification checklist and five questions to take to a tax adviser.

title: Chain Step 1 - Research Brief
usage: Define a precise research brief that can support the rest of a presentation workflow.
expected_output: A signed-off research brief with questions, boundaries, and deliverables.
tip: Resolve scope disputes now; later chain steps inherit them.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can turn an initial request into a structured and testable research brief.
prompt:
Role: You are the research lead beginning a seven-step presentation chain; produce a decision-ready brief for [TOPIC].

Review any earlier context in [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT]. Because this is step one, it may contain a rough request, stakeholder note, or “none.” Treat it as input to clarify, not as completed research. Define the intended audience [AUDIENCE], decision or learning goal [GOAL], delivery date [DEADLINE], and constraints [CONSTRAINTS].

Write a brief containing: background, central research question, five subordinate questions, in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries, required geographies and dates, key definitions, stakeholder perspectives, acceptable source types, and evidence quality rules. List assumptions separately and turn important unknowns into clarification questions.

Specify the downstream artifacts: evidence notes, synthesis, outline, slide draft, speaker notes, and final review. Add completion criteria so the next step can judge whether research coverage is adequate.

Do not research the topic yet or fabricate sources. End with a clearly labelled “HANDOFF TO STEP 2” block containing the approved brief and a compact search plan that can be pasted as [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT].

title: Chain Step 2 - Evidence Notes
usage: Convert the approved research brief into traceable, source-level evidence notes.
expected_output: An evidence ledger mapped to the brief's research questions.
tip: Save quotations with page numbers or section locations at capture time.
best_tools: Perplexity: Supports source discovery with links that can be checked against originals.
prompt:
Goal: Act as the evidence analyst for step two; complete evidence notes from the research brief in [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT].

If that input lacks scope, audience, research questions, or source standards, state what is missing and reconstruct a provisional brief from [TOPIC] before proceeding. For each supplied or discovered source [SOURCES], record author or organisation, title, date, URL or document identifier, source type, and access date.

Build notes around the brief's subordinate questions. Each note must contain one claim, a short exact quotation or precise location, relevant figures with units and period, the source's method or basis, limitations, and a relevance label. Distinguish primary evidence, analysis, opinion, and promotional content. Record contradictory findings side by side instead of forcing agreement.

Do not invent citations or imply that an inaccessible source was read. Mark weak coverage, stale evidence, and claims needing corroboration. Include a coverage matrix linking questions to sources.

Finish with “HANDOFF TO STEP 3”: a clean evidence ledger, unresolved gaps, and a list of claims safe—or unsafe—to synthesise. This handoff must stand alone when reused as [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT].

title: Chain Step 3 - Evidence Synthesis
usage: Turn verified evidence notes into findings, tensions, and calibrated implications.
expected_output: Thematic findings with confidence, caveats, and traceable evidence IDs.
tip: A synthesis should explain relationships, not merely shorten every source.
best_tools: Claude: Can compare a long evidence ledger and preserve nuanced disagreements.
prompt:
Role: You are the synthesis editor at step three; transform [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT] from evidence notes into defensible findings.

First check whether claims have source identifiers, dates, quotations or locations, and limitations. If not, flag the deficiency and avoid upgrading uncertain material. Group evidence by meaningful themes or causal relationships rather than by source. Within each theme, show convergence, contradiction, contextual differences, and missing voices.

Produce four to seven findings. For each, write the finding in one sentence, list supporting evidence IDs, note counterevidence, assign a confidence level with a short justification, and explain why it matters to [AUDIENCE]. Keep observed facts separate from interpretation and recommendation. Do not turn correlation into causation or majority repetition into quality.

Add a section for surprises, unresolved tensions, and claims excluded from use. Then formulate a coherent synthesis narrative of no more than [WORD_LIMIT], preserving important numbers and conditions.

Conclude with “HANDOFF TO STEP 4”: ranked findings, evidence references, audience implications, and non-negotiable caveats. It must be understandable independently when inserted as [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT].

title: Chain Step 4 - Presentation Outline
usage: Shape synthesised findings into a persuasive and logically paced presentation outline.
expected_output: A slide-by-slide outline with evidence mapping and timing.
tip: Give each proposed slide one job and one takeaway.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can organise findings into audience-focused narrative structures and transitions.
prompt:
Goal: Serve as the presentation architect for step four; build an outline from the synthesis in [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT].

Confirm the audience [AUDIENCE], desired outcome [OUTCOME], time available [DURATION], and delivery setting [SETTING]. If these are absent, state reasonable provisional assumptions. Choose a narrative shape—problem/response, question/answer, chronological, comparison, or another justified structure—based on the findings rather than habit.

Propose [SLIDE_COUNT] slides. For each, specify its single purpose, headline takeaway, evidence IDs to use, suitable visual form, and transition to the next idea. Include an opening that earns attention without sensationalism, a short method or evidence note, space for contradictions, and a close aligned with the requested outcome.

Check pacing against the duration and remove redundant slides. Do not draft full slide copy, design decoration, or speaker notes yet. Flag any finding that cannot be simplified without distortion.

End with “HANDOFF TO STEP 5”: the numbered slide architecture, evidence-to-slide map, visual cautions, and exact narrative through-line. Make the block complete enough to function alone as [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT].

title: Chain Step 5 - Slide Draft
usage: Draft concise slide content from an approved evidence-mapped presentation outline.
expected_output: A complete textual slide draft with source footers and visual directions.
tip: Keep nuance in evidence labels and reserve explanation for speaker notes.
best_tools: Microsoft Copilot: Can help draft presentation content within PowerPoint from a structured outline.
prompt:
Role: You are the slide writer at step five; turn the approved outline in [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT] into a restrained, evidence-faithful draft.

For every numbered slide, create a short assertion-style title and only the minimum body copy needed for [AUDIENCE] to grasp the takeaway. Prefer one visual idea over stacked bullet lists. Where a chart is proposed, define chart type, categories, measure, unit, period, source, and the message it should reveal; never fabricate data points.

Add source footers using the evidence IDs supplied. Preserve confidence labels and caveats where omission could mislead. Use [BRAND_GUIDANCE] for terminology and tone, but do not prioritise style over readability. Include an accessible text alternative for each substantive visual.

Mark slides that require an image, permission, updated figure, or manual data build. Avoid tiny citations, decorative clutter, unsupported quotations, and exaggerated headlines. Keep detailed explanation out of slide bodies.

Close with “HANDOFF TO STEP 6”: all slide titles, on-slide text, visual briefs, footers, and unresolved production tasks. The handoff must work as standalone [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT] for speaker-note creation.

title: Chain Step 6 - Speaker Notes
usage: Create natural speaker notes that add context without reading the slides aloud.
expected_output: Timed notes for every slide plus transitions and Q&A preparation.
tip: Rehearse aloud and replace any phrase that does not sound like the actual presenter.
best_tools: Claude: Can maintain narrative continuity across a complete slide draft and its evidence context.
prompt:
Goal: Act as the presentation coach for step six; write speaker notes for the slide draft contained in [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT].

Use the presenter's voice [VOICE], audience knowledge [AUDIENCE_LEVEL], and total duration [DURATION]. For each slide, provide an opening sentence, the explanation that is not already visible, evidence nuance, a natural transition, and an estimated speaking time. Expand abbreviations on first use and give pronunciation cues for unfamiliar names where verified.

Notes should sound spoken, not like an essay. Preserve uncertainty and explain chart denominators or baselines that audiences may miss. Add a pause or interaction cue only when it advances the goal. Never introduce new facts without an evidence reference; mark unsupported additions [VERIFY].

Prepare five likely questions, concise evidence-based responses, and an honest fallback for questions outside the research. Include reminders for accessibility, remote delivery, or handouts from [SETTING].

Finish with “HANDOFF TO STEP 7”: the slide-linked notes, timing total, Q&A sheet, and all [VERIFY] items. Ensure this block can be reviewed independently as [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT].

title: Chain Step 7 - Final Quality Review
usage: Conduct a final evidence, narrative, design, accessibility, and delivery review.
expected_output: A prioritised issue log, corrected items, and a release decision.
tip: A human owner should resolve every critical issue and rehearse the corrected deck.
best_tools: ChatGPT: Can apply a structured multi-criterion review to slides and speaker notes.
prompt:
Role: You are the independent quality reviewer for the final chain step; audit the presentation package in [PREVIOUS_OUTPUT] before release.

Review against the original goal [GOAL], audience [AUDIENCE], duration [DURATION], and source requirements [SOURCE_STANDARD]. If earlier artifacts are missing, list the resulting review limits. Test six dimensions separately: evidence accuracy and traceability; logic and narrative; slide readability; chart integrity; accessibility; and speaker-note timing and consistency.

Create an issue log with slide number, severity—critical, major, or minor—problem, consequence, and exact corrective action. Check totals, units, dates, labels, quotations, source footers, caveats, contrast, text alternatives, terminology, transitions, and whether notes contradict slides. Identify any claim that exceeds its evidence.

Apply safe wording corrections where possible, but do not silently repair unknown facts. Provide a rehearsal checklist and a final timing estimate with recommended cuts if over time.

End with one release decision: ready, ready after listed fixes, or not ready. Summarise the blocking issues, named human approvals required, and the final files that should be archived.
